business_problem: Wanxing Technology needed to reduce the cost of API-based video generation, gain more control over model quality, and secure enough AI compute to support very high global demand for AIGC video features.
solution_summary: Wanxing Technology partnered with Huawei Cloud to replace costly external API-based generation with a unified AI-and-cloud foundation for its video-creation products. Ascend AI Cloud Service supplies the training and inference compute base, while the Pangu multimodal large model provides the generative layer used to build Wanxing Tianmu 2.0. On top of that foundation, Tianmu 2.0 exposes six controllable video capabilities: image-to-video, video continuation from first and last frames, reference-based generation, controllable video generation, video editing, and audio-video synchronization. User prompts, images, and video frames are fed into the multimodal pipeline, which produces motion-controlled clips and synchronized sound effects for creative applications. The architecture is built for very high throughput because Wanxing says its AIGC products already see more than one million video-generation requests per day.

data_flow: Text prompts, first and last frames, and reference assets enter Tianmu 2.0 on top of the Pangu multimodal model and Ascend compute, where the system generates or extends video, edits motion, and synchronizes audio. The outputs are then served into Wanxing's AIGC creative software portfolio for end users.
business_outcome: The project gave Wanxing a proprietary AIGC video-creation platform with controllable generation features and a path away from expensive third-party video APIs, while scaling the model foundation for global creative products.
